title: Spelling your name
canDo: spell your name and follow someone spelling theirs

dialogue.setting: Priya is opening a bank account in Sudbury, Ontario. The bank advisor, Hélène, writes down her name.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.fr: Bonjour. Votre nom, s'il vous plaît ?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.en: Sharma… How do you spell that?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: S, H, A, R, M, A.
lines.en: S, H, A, R, M, A.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.fr: P, R, I, i grec, A ?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: Oui, c'est ça. Et vous, comment vous appelez-vous ?
lines.en: Yes, that's right. And you, what's your name?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.fr: Hélène Bélanger. B, E accent aigu, L, A, N, G, E, R.
lines.en: Hélène Bélanger. B, E with an acute accent, L, A, N, G, E, R.

vocabulary.note: Literally "It's written how?" Very common in everyday speech.
The accent on è, à and ù.
The accent on ê, â, î, ô and û.
The two dots on ë and ï, as in Noël.

grammar.title: The alphabet
explanation: French uses the same 26 letters as English, but most of the letter names sound different. Here they are, with a rough English sound for each:

A (ah), B (bay), C (say), D (day), E (uh), F (eff), G (zhay), H (ash), I (ee), J (zhee), K (kah), L (ell), M (em), N (en), O (oh), P (pay), Q (kü), R (air, with the French r), S (ess), T (tay), U (ü), V (vay), W (doo-bluh-vay), X (eeks), Y (ee-grek), Z (zed).
ü is not an English sound: say "ee", then round your lips as if for "oo" without moving your tongue.
To spell a letter with an accent, say the letter and then the accent: é is « e accent aigu », ç is « c cédille ».

examples.fr: B, E accent aigu, L, A, N, G, E, R
P, R, I, i grec, A

pronunciation.sound: Letter names: e, i, g, j
explanation: English speakers often mix up four letter names. In French, E sounds like "uh" and I sounds like "ee".
G sounds like "zhay" and J like "zhee". Both start with the sound in the middle of "measure".
They end the opposite way from English: the French G ends like the English letter J ("jay"), and the French J ends like the English letter G ("jee").

examples.fr: R, E accent aigu, M, I
